thread:
maria_sales: Hey team — large enterprise (FinCo) wants our CAIQ back by EOD Friday. Two asks: 1) clarification on shared responsibility for logging/KMS during a POC, 2) whether Dedicated/reserved pricing is required to meet their SLA (they asked about throughput & billing). Any quick notes I can paste into the SIG response?

trent_sec: @maria_sales short answer: for hosted POC we own app-layer controls and platform-level controls; customer owns tenant data classification, access provisioning, and customer-managed keys if they choose BYOE. For CAIQ mapping, mark CCM controls around "Logging and Monitoring" as shared — we collect infra logs, they must retain their audit trails for app-level events.

maria_sales: Can you be more specific for the CAIQ fields? They asked which questions we mark as "red" vs "shared".

trent_sec: Sure — examples: 
- CCM:LOG-01 (Collection of system logs) => Redwood: responsible for collection and retention of infrastructure logs (hosted platform). 
- CCM:LOG-02 (Application logging) => Customer: responsible for instrumenting their app; Redwood can forward logs to customer endpoint on request. 
- CCM:KEY-03 (KMS Management) => If customer uses BYOK/BYOE (tenant KMS) => Customer owns key lifecycle; if not, Redwood manages keys (we provide HSM-backed KMS).

devon_eng: For the POC environment we can spin up a dedicated tenant in hosted; we can enable cross-account log delivery (S3 bucket + event notification). If they want end-to-end evidence for SIG artifacts we can provide: delivery proof (S3 ACLs), access logs (CloudTrail-style entries), and a short playbook of how we isolate the tenant during the POC.

maria_sales: Perfect. Any snippet I can paste into the CAIQ "Shared Responsibility" free-text field?

trent_sec: Paste this: "Redwood is responsible for the security and operation of the inference platform (compute, network, platform services). The customer is responsible for data and access controls within their tenant, including customer-managed keys where BYOE is selected, application-level logging, and secrets within their models. Where controls overlap (e.g., log forwarding, retention), Redwood and the customer coordinate via documented handoff: Redwood exports infra logs and provides delivery endpoints; the customer manages retention and analysis. Specific evidence artifacts available for POC: exported infra logs, tenant audit events, KMS access audit trails, and network flow captures on request."

sam_platform: On pricing: for a POC with predictable throughput under 10 r/s we can run hosted, but note higher per-token rates for on-demand. If they want sustained latency SLAs or guaranteed concurrency we should propose Dedicated (reserved capacity) — that moves billing from per-token to committed monthly GPU capacity. I can attach a quick TCO calc.

maria_sales: They specifically asked if using customer KMS increases costs or requires Dedicated.

trent_sec: BYOE itself doesn't force Dedicated. It does require some integration work (KMS PRs, key policies, validation). We typically treat customer-managed KMS as an access control boundary: we need to validate key import, set IAM policies, and run an attestation. The extra engineering for onboarding is a one-time effort; it does not change runtime pricing.

devon_eng: Implementation notes to the SIG:
```
- For BYOE: customer creates key in their KMS and grants a service principal principal:GetPublicKey, Encrypt/Decrypt for the Redwood tenant role.
- We do not persist plaintext keys. We use the KMS for envelope encryption of model artifacts and tenant secrets.
- We log all KMS API calls and can provide the KMS audit stream as evidence.
```

maria_sales: Great. They also want to know what evidence files we can attach to the CAIQ zip.

trent_sec: We can provide: 
- Tenant audit log extract (JSON)
- Infra logs (redacted) showing the POC timeframe
- KMS access audit trail (if BYOE enabled)
- Network diagram and ephemeral IP allocation list for the POC
- Short config snippet showing RBAC roles applied to the tenant

sam_platform: I'll add a note in the pricing section: "BYOE onboarding may incur professional services if they need Redwood to perform key rotation or KMS account setup on their behalf — otherwise self-serve is free."

maria_sales: One more: timeline — they need the SIG back Friday but also want a short 30m sync tomorrow to confirm evidence attachments. Who can join?

devon_eng: I can do 11:30am PT.

trent_sec: I'll join at 11:30 and bring the CAIQ field mapping.

sam_platform: I can do 11:30 for pricing context.

maria_sales: Awesome — scheduled. I'll paste your snippets into the CAIQ free-text and attach the artifacts list. Thanks! :thumbsup:

security-bot: SIG submission checklist: CAIQ JSON attached? (no) Evidence ZIP attached? (pending) Approver assigned: @trent_sec. Submit by 2029-11-22 23:59 UTC to meet customer deadline.
